title: Tenant traffic curation and dynamic quota hedging
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Background: As Dedicated customers scale, we need deterministic throughput guarantees while avoiding costly over-provisioning. Current fleet behavior shows tail latency spikes when a single tenant produces bursty long-context workloads; these noisy neighbors reduce effective throughput for co-tenants and cause SLA violations. Goal: introduce a tenant traffic curation layer plus a dynamic quota-hedging mechanism that lets us provide per-tenant throughput contracts while allowing short, predictable bursts and automatic, measurable graceful degradation when capacity pressure is sustained.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Per-tenant throughput contracts enforced for 95% of 1h windows within +/-10% of target under representative workload mix (chat+completion+embedding), validated in staging.
2) Noisy-neighbor-induced p50/p95 latency regressions for co-tenants reduced by >=40% in mixed-workload tests compared to baseline (current scheduler), measured on the fx-fleet-qa cluster.

3) Autoscaler interactions: when autoscale cannot provision capacity within configured headroom window, system applies progressive backpressure and hedged quota actions without dropping in-flight requests >0.5% of cases.
4) Observability: Console surfaces per-tenant quota debt, eviction score, and predicted time-to-recover on rollout dashboard; alerting thresholds added to runtime SLO alerts.
5) Playbook: documented operational steps for forced-quota reconciliation, tenant pause/resume, and customer-facing incident messaging in Confluence.
6) Security review complete for telemetry and cross-tenant metrics; no plaintext tenant identifiers in logs.
7) End-to-end e2e test and a canary rollout plan ready for release candidate.
8) Performance regressions: end-to-end token throughput on production-like hardware must not regress more than 5% for steady-state workloads after fencing turned on.
9) Rollback plan validated (automatic feature flag toggle) with a maximum rollback window of 30 minutes for global fleet changes.
tasks: Design: traffic curation spec (admission control, token buckets, short-burst credits, eviction scoring). Create Confluence doc.
Prototype: implement admission controller in the request gateway with per-tenant token buckets and short-burst credits (feature-branch).
Scheduler integration: extend lane allocator to support fenced lanes and quota debt accounting; add eviction score computation to scheduler.
Autoscale hooks: add headroom signals and hedging API so autoscaler can request temporary capacity loan and record debts.
Observability: new metrics (tenant_quota_used, tenant_quota_debt, eviction_score, short_burst_consumed). Dashboard and alerts.
E2E tests: create mixed-workload test harness, add noisy-neighbor scenario and regression tests to CI (staging cluster).
Canary: deploy to a small set of tenants on dedicated-qa and run soak for 72 hours with telemetry review.
Docs & Playbook: update Console runtime docs, create incident runbook, and customer-facing KB article for quota behavior.

decisions: Use a hybrid enforcement model: soft token-bucket quotas with a bounded short-burst credit and eviction-score-driven partial preemption. This balances customer experience and resource utilization.

Autoscaler will expose a 'loan' API for temporary capacity; loans create a recorded debt that triggers prioritized provisioning and, if unpaid, leads to progressive throttling for the tenant that borrowed capacity.
Per-tenant 'strict' contracts will map to hard reservations (no hedging) and require explicit capacity allocation via Dedicated purchase flow; default contracts use hedging.
Telemetry will not include plaintext tenant IDs in exported artifacts; a hashed tenant identifier will be used for cross-trace correlation.

Fallback policy: when fencing is triggered and degradation persists beyond threshold, requests will be routed to a compatible model variant (smaller quantized model) if available before outright rejection.
